minutes.headline: Joint boards interviewed two planning board applicants; most school-project site waivers were granted, curbing one held.
minutes.summary: The joint Planning Board and Selectmen session interviewed two applicants for a planning board seat, with the appointment to be voted at the selectmen's meeting the next night. The Planning Board then took an ANR plan for Holman Street and went through the waiver list for the combined middle/high school project item by item, granting most, denying one granite curb waiver at Oak Avenue and holding another. It also approved minutes and a temporary banner, and scheduled the village charette and master plan feedback.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board went through the waiver list for the combined middle/high school project item by item, approving most with conditions.
A granite curb waiver at Oak Avenue was not granted, and the granite curb item 17 was put on hold pending research on Mass Ave entrances.
Height and sign waivers are to be run by the building inspector; the other waivers were approved with conditions.
Joint boards interviewed two planning board applicants; the appointment is to be voted at the selectmen's meeting the next night.
An ANR plan for Holman Street was referred to departments and is due back July 28; a temporary banner at the Walmart plaza was approved.

why_it_matters: Curb type, drainage design and sign size on the school project affect what the building costs and how stormwater is handled near Mass Ave, and the minutes record that stormwater changes added to construction cost.
The open waiver on granite curbs and the unresolved culvert question could still change the project's design and cost, and the town budget, mostly taxes, would carry any change.
watch_next: July 28 regular meeting, when the Holman Street ANR plan returns and the held granite curb item may be taken up.
July 30 village district bylaw charette, and the selectmen's vote on the planning board appointment the night after this meeting.

reconciliation.summary: The two records overlap on the Spirit Halloween banner, the waiver items, the July 30 charette and the main board members, but differ on several details. The main thing to know is that ours calls the banner vote inaudible and puts it at Walmart, while the official records it as passed unanimously at 301 Massachusetts Avenue. Waiver #17 is also described differently: ours says on hold, the official says not granted.
